# Planetary Moon Count Comparison

This report compares the known number of moons orbiting Jupiter, Saturn, and Mars based on the latest available data.

## Summary of Moon Counts

| Planet | Moon Count | Data Source Date | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Saturn** | 293 | June 2026 | Saturn has the highest count among the three planets. |
| **Jupiter** | 115 | April 2026 | Jupiter is the second most numerous in this comparison. |
| **Mars** | 2 | N/A | Mars has only two small, irregularly shaped moons: Phobos and Deimos. |

## Detailed Comparison

**Saturn**
Saturn boasts the largest number of known moons in this comparison, with 293 officially recognized satellites as of June 2026. Its moons include notable bodies like Titan, which possesses its own atmosphere.

**Jupiter**
Jupiter has 115 known moons. This massive count reflects the giant nature of the planet and the complexity of its satellite system.

**Mars**
Mars has a significantly smaller satellite system, possessing only two moons: Phobos and Deimos. These moons are small and are believed to be captured asteroids.

## Conclusion

The data clearly shows a massive difference in the number of moons between the gas giants (Jupiter and Saturn) and the terrestrial planet (Mars). Saturn currently leads the comparison with 293 moons, followed by Jupiter with 115, and Mars with only 2.

# Planetary Moon Count Comparison

This report compares the known number of moons orbiting Jupiter, Saturn, and Mars based on the latest available data.

## Summary of Moon Counts

| Planet | Moon Count | Data Source Date | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Saturn** | 293 | June 2026 | Saturn has the highest count among the three planets. |
| **Jupiter** | 115 | April 2026 | Jupiter is the second most numerous in this comparison. |
| **Mars** | 2 | N/A | Mars has only two small, irregularly shaped moons: Phobos and Deimos. |

## Detailed Comparison

**Saturn**
Saturn boasts the largest number of known moons in this comparison, with 293 officially recognized satellites as of June 2026. Its moons include notable bodies like Titan, which possesses its own atmosphere.

**Jupiter**
Jupiter has 115 known moons. This massive count reflects the giant nature of the planet and the complexity of its satellite system.

**Mars**
Mars has a significantly smaller satellite system, possessing only two moons: Phobos and Deimos. These moons are small and are believed to be captured asteroids.

## Conclusion

The data clearly shows a massive difference in the number of moons between the gas giants (Jupiter and Saturn) and the terrestrial planet (Mars). Saturn currently leads the comparison with 293 moons, followed by Jupiter with 115, and Mars with only 2.
